name.text: Forming and solving an inequality in one unknown

questiontext.text:
[[if test="is(kind=\"load\")"]]A fishing boat on Lake Victoria can carry a load of at most {@L@} kg. The fisherman and his nets weigh {@F@} kg. Crates of fish weigh {@w@} kg each. Let \(n\) be the number of crates.[[elif test="is(kind=\"budget\")"]]Nekesa has Ksh {@L@}. She pays Ksh {@F@} to enter the Nairobi Agricultural Show and spends the rest on rides at Ksh {@w@} each. Let \(n\) be the number of rides.[[elif test="is(kind=\"lift\")"]]A goods lift can carry at most {@L@} kg. A worker and her trolley weigh {@F@} kg. Boxes of paper weigh {@w@} kg each. Let \(n\) be the number of boxes.[[elif test="is(kind=\"boda\")"]]A boda boda rider pays Ksh {@F@} a day for fuel and the bike's hire. He earns Ksh {@w@} for each trip and wants a profit of at least Ksh {@L@} in a day. Let \(n\) be the number of trips.[[elif test="is(kind=\"savings\")"]]Baraka has saved Ksh {@F@}. He saves Ksh {@w@} every week and wants at least Ksh {@L@} for a bicycle. Let \(n\) be the number of weeks.[[else]]A mama mboga pays Ksh {@F@} a day for her stall. She makes a profit of Ksh {@w@} on each bunch of sukuma wiki and wants a profit of at least Ksh {@L@} in a day. Let \(n\) be the number of bunches.[[/if]]

(a) Write an inequality in \(n\).

[[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] [[feedback:prt1]]

(b) Solve your inequality. Give the exact value.

\(n\) [[input:ans2]] [[input:ans3]] [[validation:ans3]] [[feedback:prt2]]

(c) What is the [[if test="is(rel=\"le\")"]]greatest[[else]]least[[/if]] number of {@item@}?

[[input:ans4]] {@item@} [[validation:ans4]] [[feedback:prt3]]

generalfeedback.text:
(a) The total {@totw@} is \({@tot@}\)[[if test="earn"]] (the earnings minus the daily cost)[[/if]], and it must be [[if test="is(rel=\"le\")"]]at most[[else]]at least[[/if]] \({@L@}\): \({@ta1@}\). A solved form such as {@ansd@} is also a correct inequality in \(n\).

(b) [[if test="earn"]]Add \({@F@}\) to[[else]]Subtract \({@F@}\) from[[/if]] both sides: \({@w@}n {@relt(rel)@} {@bnd*w@}\). Divide both sides by \({@w@}\), a positive number, so the sign stays the same: {@ansd@}.

(c) \(n\) must be a whole number. [[if test="is(rel=\"le\")"]]The greatest whole number that is at most \({@nd(bnd)@}\) is \({@ans4t@}\); \({@ans4t+1@}\) {@item@} would be too many.[[else]]The least whole number that is at least \({@nd(bnd)@}\) is \({@ans4t@}\); \({@ans4t-1@}\) {@item@} would not be enough.[[/if]] Check: with \(n = {@ans4t@}\) the total is \({@ev(tot,n=ans4t)@}\); with \(n = {@wrongr@}\) it is \({@ev(tot,n=wrongr)@}\).

[[if test="is(rel=\"le\")"]]At most includes \({@L@}\) itself, so use \(\le\).[[else]]At least includes \({@L@}\) itself, so use \(\ge\).[[/if]]
You left out the \({@F@}\): the total {@totw@} includes it.

truefeedback.text: Test your number: with \(n = {@wrongr@}\) the total {@totw@} is \({@ev(tot,n=wrongr)@}\), which is [[if test="is(rel=\"le\")"]]more than \({@L@}\): too many {@item@}.[[else]]less than \({@L@}\): not enough {@item@}.[[/if]] \(n\) must be a whole number that satisfies your inequality.
That is the right whole number for your answer to (b), but (b) is not right.
